t: Find Products of Elements of Big Array
o: big_nums concatenates the binary representation's set bits (as powers of two, ascending) of 1, 2, 3, …. Each set bit of integer i is one 'entry' whose value is 2^b; the product of a positional range is therefore 2 raised to the sum of the bit-indices of the entries in that range. With positions up to 10^15 we work purely with prefix counting: for each bit b, the count of integers ≤ x having bit b set is a closed-form floor expression, giving prefix sums F(x) = number of entries ≤ position x and G(x) = Σ of entry exponents before position x. Per query, binary-search the boundary integers and combine partial tails/heads with the G-difference of the interior. Check: positions 1..3 hold 2,1,2 → exponents 1,0,1 → 2² = 4 ✓.
k: big_nums is exactly the concatenated set-bit multiset of 1, 2, 3, …; a product over a range is 2^(sum of entry bit-indices).
Count of integers ≤ x with bit b set has an O(1) closed form, enabling prefix sums F (entry counts) and G (exponent sums) without materializing anything.
Each query needs the two boundary integers (via binary search on F) plus partial tail/head sums; the interior is G(x1−1) − G(x0).

a.n: Approach 1: Bit-count prefixes + boundary binary search
a.i: Define cb(b, x) = #{i ≤ x : bit b of i is 1} via the standard digit formula. Then F(x) = Σ_b cb(b,x) counts entries and G(x) = Σ_b b·cb(b,x) sums their exponents. Locate x0 (integer containing position 'from') and x1 (containing 'to') by binary search on F; the answer exponent is the tail of x0's set bits, plus G(x1−1) − G(x0) for the interior, plus the head of x1's set bits.
s: Implement cb(b, x), F(x) = Σ cb, G(x) = Σ b·cb, and setBits(x).
Binary search x0 = min{x : F(x) > from} and x1 = min{x : F(x) > to}.
Exponent = sum(setBits(x0)[s0:]) + (G(x1−1) − G(x0) if x1 > x0+1) + sum(setBits(x1)[:t1]), handling x1 == x0 by slicing directly.
a.t: O(Q · log(maxPos) · 50) — two binary searches per query, each evaluating 51-term prefix sums.

w: The crucial insight is that products become powers of two, so only exponent sums matter — no big-number multiplication anywhere. Pitfalls: the x1 == x0 case (both partials live in the same integer — slice, don't double count), off-by-one in F/G definitions (decide whether the prefix includes position x and stay consistent), and mod = 1 (everything is 0). Follow-up: sum (instead of product) of range elements, or answer position lookups big_nums[p] directly (binary search on F, then read the s0-th set bit).
